content: In 1803, Giovanni Battista Monteggia, an Italian surgeon, described the Monteggia fracture as a fracture of the proximal third of the ulna accompanied by a dislocation of the radial head. In 1967, Jose Luis Bado introduced the term Monteggia lesion and classified this injury into four distinct types. In 1991, Jupiter JB and colleagues from Boston expanded upon Bado’s classification, specifically elaborating on the description of the posterior Monteggia fracture-dislocation, which corresponds to Bado’s Type II classification.
